items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I always thought, if he wanted to, he could play like Earl Hines, on that style.

ctx.x: But until he made that speech, everything was great. They tolerated him. But with that speech, it's funny how that -- everything turned around and he was walking frontwards and all that, just with Johnny shaking him. I got the story from Earl Wiley. I wasn't there at the time. Tut was working there. But it was that kind of a place, where they let you -- one time, Earl Wiley drank to excess many times. When he drank, he drank to excess. And then he couldn't play, and he knew it.

And then you had to follow him. They loved him there. So that, one of the bosses would send -- or do it themselves, see what Earl would do, because Earl would break down his drums. That's a modern term, tear down his drums. And pawn them so he'd get enough money. And they'd follow him and get the pawn tickets, and redeem them there, and he'd be working -- you know he'd been working . But he'd just get so drunk, that this one night, Dave T ough was visiting. And it was early in the evening. Earl was upstairs…
